The other lamb you shall offer at twilight, preparing the same meal offering and libation as in the morning—an offering by fire of pleasing odor to the L<small>ORD</small>.

en: On your new moons you shall present a burnt offering to the L<small>ORD</small>: two bulls of the herd, one ram, and seven yearling lambs, without blemish.
As meal offering for each bull: three-tenths of a measure of choice flour with oil mixed in. As meal offering for each ram: two-tenths of a measure of choice flour with oil mixed in.
As meal offering for each lamb: a tenth of a measure of fine flour with oil mixed in. Such shall be the burnt offering of pleasing odor, an offering by fire to the L<small>ORD</small>.
Their libations shall be: half a hin of wine for a bull, a third of a hin for a ram, and a quarter of a hin for a lamb. That shall be the monthly burnt offering for each new moon of the year.
And there shall be one goat as a sin offering to the L<small>ORD</small>, to be offered in addition to the regular burnt offering and its libation.

en: the regular burnt offering instituted at Mount Sinai—an offering by fire of pleasing odor to the L<small>ORD</small>.
The libation with it shall be a quarter of a hin for each lamb, to be poured in the sacred precinct as an offering of fermented drink to the LORD.
The other lamb you shall offer at twilight, preparing the same meal offering and libation as in the morning—an offering by fire of pleasing odor to the L<small>ORD</small>.
On the sabbath day: two yearling lambs without blemish, together with two-tenths of a measure of choice flour with oil mixed in as a meal offering, and with the proper libation—

en: On your new moons you shall present a burnt offering to the L<small>ORD</small>: two bulls of the herd, one ram, and seven yearling lambs, without blemish.
As meal offering for each bull: three-tenths of a measure of choice flour with oil mixed in. As meal offering for each ram: two-tenths of a measure of choice flour with oil mixed in.
As meal offering for each lamb: a tenth of a measure of fine flour with oil mixed in. Such shall be the burnt offering of pleasing odor, an offering by fire to the L<small>ORD</small>.
Their libations shall be: half a hin of wine for a bull, a third of a hin for a ram, and a quarter of a hin for a lamb. That shall be the monthly burnt offering for each new moon of the year.
And there shall be one goat as a sin offering to the L<small>ORD</small>, to be offered in addition to the regular burnt offering and its libation.

comments.en: העשיה בהר סיני WHICH WAS OFFERED BY MOUNT SINAI — i.e., like those continual burnt offerings which were offered during the days of the installation ceremony (which took place whilst the people were encamped by Mount Sinai). — Another explanation of העשיה בהר סיני is: It compares the continual burnt offering to the burnt offering of Mount Sinai — to that which was offered on the fifth day of the third month, before the Giving of the Torah (see Rashi on Exodus 19:11), of which it is written, (Exodus 24:6) “And he put it (the blood) in basins”: this teaches, therefore, that it (the continual burnt-offering) requires a vessel for the reception of the blood (Sifra, Tzav, Chapter 18 8).
Moses took one part of the blood and put it in basins, and the other part of the blood he dashed against the altar.

en: The L<small>ORD</small> spoke to Moses, saying:
Command the Israelite people and say to them: Be punctilious in presenting to Me at stated times the offerings of food due Me, as offerings by fire of pleasing odor to Me.

Say to them: These are the offerings by fire that you are to present to the LORD:
As a regular burnt offering every day, two yearling lambs without blemish.

As a regular burnt offering every day, two yearling lambs without blemish.

en: the regular burnt offering instituted at Mount Sinai—an offering by fire of pleasing odor to the L<small>ORD</small>.
The libation with it shall be a quarter of a hin for each lamb, to be poured in the sacred precinct as an offering of fermented drink to the LORD.
The other lamb you shall offer at twilight, preparing the same meal offering and libation as in the morning—an offering by fire of pleasing odor to the L<small>ORD</small>.
On the sabbath day: two yearling lambs without blemish, together with two-tenths of a measure of choice flour with oil mixed in as a meal offering, and with the proper libation—
a burnt offering for every sabbath, in addition to the regular burnt offering and its libation.

en: On your new moons you shall present a burnt offering to the L<small>ORD</small>: two bulls of the herd, one ram, and seven yearling lambs, without blemish.
As meal offering for each bull: three-tenths of a measure of choice flour with oil mixed in. As meal offering for each ram: two-tenths of a measure of choice flour with oil mixed in.
As meal offering for each lamb: a tenth of a measure of fine flour with oil mixed in. Such shall be the burnt offering of pleasing odor, an offering by fire to the L<small>ORD</small>.
Their libations shall be: half a hin of wine for a bull, a third of a hin for a ram, and a quarter of a hin for a lamb. That shall be the monthly burnt offering for each new moon of the year.
And there shall be one goat as a sin offering to the L<small>ORD</small>, to be offered in addition to the regular burnt offering and its libation.

comments.en: The kohen reads three verses, which are "And he said," "Command," and "And say" (Numbers 28:1-3). The levite returns to reading "And say," and then reads "The first sheep" and "A tenth of an ephah" (Numbers 28:3-5). The Israelite reads from "The regular offering" up to "And on your new moons" (Numbers 28:6-10). And the fourth reads from "And on your new moons" to the end (Numbers 28:11-15).

comments.en: נטף is balsam. Because it is merely the sap which drips from the wood of the balsam tree it is called נטף, “dripping” (Keritot 6a). In old French it is called gomme; English gum. The balm itself, however, is called thériaque (cf., however, Ramban).

comments.he: נטף. הוּא צֳרִי, וְעַל שֶׁאֵינוֹ אֶלָּא שְׂרָף הַנּוֹטֵף מֵעֲצֵי הַקְּטָף קָרוּי נָטָף, וּבְלַעַז גומ"א, וְהַצֳּרִי קוֹרִין לוֹ טרי"אקה:

comments.en: ושחלת AND ONYCHA This is a root of a fragrant herb, smooth and transparent like a fingernail, In the language of the Mishna it is called צפורן, a nail (cf. Keritot 6a). This is exactly how Onkelos renders it: וטופרא, which is the Aramaic word corresponding to the Hebrew צפורן‎.

comments.he: ושחלת. שֹׁרֶשׁ בֹּשֶׁם חָלָק וּמַצְהִיר כְּצִּפֹּרֶן, וּבִלְשׁוֹן הַמִּשְׁנָה קָרוּי צִפֹּרֶן, וְזֶהוּ שֶׁתִּרְגֵּם אֻנְקְלוֹס וְטוּפְרָא:

comments.en: וחלבנה — This is a malodorous spice which is called galbanum. Scripture enumerates it among the spices of the incense to teach us that we should not regard as a light thing the duty of associating with ourselves when we band together for fasts and prayers Israelites who are transgressors — that they should be counted as ourselves (Keritot 6b).

comments.he: וחלבנה. בֹּשֶׂם שֶׁרֵיחוֹ רַע, וְקוֹרִין לוֹ גַלְבְּנָא, וּמְנָאָהּ הַכָּתוּב בֵּין סַמָּנֵי הַקְּטֹרֶת לְלַמְּדֵנוּ שֶׁלֹּא יֵקַל בְּעֵינֵינוּ לְצָרֵף עִמָּנוּ בַּאֲגֻדַּת תַּעֲנִיּוֹתֵינוּ וּתְפִלּוֹתֵנוּ אֶת פּוֹשְׁעֵי יִשְׂרָאֵל שֶׁיִּהְיוּ נִמְנִין עִמָּנוּ:

comments.en: סמים means other SPICES also.

comments.he: סמים. אֲחֵרִים:

comments.en: ולבנה זכה AND PURE FRANKINCENSE — From here our Rabbis learned that eleven spices were mentioned to Moses on Sinai (a technical term, like הלכה למשה מסיני) as the ingredients of the incense. For the least number implied by the plural סמים is two; balsam, onycha and galbanum are three, making together five. The word סמים that follows (without stating any number) is intended to add a similar number as these already prescribed, viz., five, making ten, and frankincense makes eleven. They are the following: balm, onycha, galbanum, frankincense, myrrh, cassia, spikenard and saffron, altogether eight — for שבלת and נרד are one, it being given this compound name only because the nard resembles a שבלת, a spike, — costus, aromatic bark and cinnamon, altogether eleven. “Borith karshina” (lye obtained from a species of vetch) which is also mentioned in Keritotot 6a in connection with the ingredients of the incense was not burnt itself as incense, but the onycha was rubbed with it in order to whiten it — that it should be (look) better (Keritot 6a).

comments.he: ולבנה זכה. מִכָּאן לָמְדוּ רַבּוֹתֵינוּ י"א סַמָּנִין נֶאֶמְרוּ לוֹ לְמֹשֶׁה בְּסִינַי – מִעוּט סַמִּים שְׁנַיִם, נָטָף וּשְׁחֵלֶת וְחֶלְבְּנָה ג', הֲרֵי חֲמִשָּׁה, סַמִּים לְרַבּוֹת עוֹד כְּמוֹ אֵלּוּ הֲרֵי עֲשָׂרָה, וּלְבוֹנָה הֲרֵי י"א; וְאֵלּוּ הֵן הַצֳּרִי וְהַצִּפֹּרֶן הַחֶלְבְּנָה וְהַלְּבוֹנָה מֹר וּקְצִיעָה שִׁבֹּלֶת נֵרְדְּ וְכַרְכֹּם הֲרֵי ח' – שֶׁהַשִּׁבֹּלֶת וְנֵרְדְּ אֶחָד, שֶׁהַנֵּרְדְּ דּוֹמֶה לְשִׁבֹּלֶת – הַקֹּשְׁטְ וְהַקִּלּוּפָה וְקִנָּמוֹן הֲרֵי י"א; בֹּרִית כַּרְשִׁינָה אֵינוֹ נִקְטָר אֶלָּא בּוֹ שָׁפִין אֶת הַצִּפֹּרֶן לְלַבְּנָהּ שֶׁתְּהֵא נָאָה (כריתות ו'):

comments.en: בד בבד יהיה means, these four ingredients mentioned here shall be equal, weight for weight — as the weight of one so shall be the weight of another. Thus indeed we learn (Keritot 6a): the balm, the onycha, the galbanum and the frankincense shall each have the weight of seventy manehs. The term בד seems to me to mean “a single article” (cf. בָּדָד, לְבַד) – they shall be “one equal with one”: they shall be the one the same as the other.

comments.he: בד בבד יהיה. אֵלּוּ הָאַרְבָּעָה הַנִּזְכָּרִים כָּאן יִהְיוּ שָׁוִין מִשְׁקָל בְּמִשְׁקָל – כְּמִשְׁקָלוֹ שֶׁל זֶה כָּךְ מִשְׁקָלוֹ שֶׁל זֶה – וְכֵן שָׁנִינוּ: הַצֳּרִי וְהַצִּפֹּרֶן הַחֶלְבְּנָה וְהַלְּבוֹנָה מִשְׁקַל שִׁבְעִים שִׁבְעִים מָנֶה (שם); וּלְשׁוֹן בַּד נִרְאֶה בְעֵינַי שֶׁהוּא לְשׁוֹן יָחִיד, אֶחָד בְּאֶחָד יִהְיוּ – זֶה כְּמוֹת זֶה:

comments.en: ממלח TEMPERED TOGETHER — Understand this as the Targum renders it: מעורב, mixed — that they should thoroughly intermix the powder of the ingredients. I think that similar in meaning to it are the nouns in (Jona 1:5) “Then the mariners (המלחים) were afraid”; (Ezekiel 27:27) “thy mariners (מלחיך) and thy pilots”, who are so called because they turn over (stir up) the water with oars when they propel the ship — like a person who stirs up beaten eggs with a spoon in order to mix them with water. Anything that a person wishes to mix up thoroughly he stirs up with his finger or with a spoon.

Your wealth, your wares, your merchandise,
Your sailors and your pilots,
The men who made your repairs,
Those who carried on your traffic,
And all the fighting men within you—
All the multitude within you—

comments.en: ונתת ממנה וגו׳ AND THOU SHALT PUT OF IT [BEFORE THE TESTIMONY IN THE APPOINTED TENT] — This refers to the incense which was burnt daily on the inner altar that was in the tent of meeting.

comments.he: ונתתה ממנה וגו'. הִיא קְטֹרֶת שֶׁבְּכָל יוֹם וָיוֹם שֶׁעַל מִזְבֵּחַ הַפְּנִימִי שֶׁהוּא בְאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד:

comments.en: אשר אועד לך שמה WHERE I WILL BE MET BY THEE — All appointments for the purpose of speaking unto you which I shall make with you I shall confine to that place (cf. Rashi on Exodus 25:22).

comments.he: אשר אועד לך שמה. כָּל מוֹעֲדֵי דִּבּוּר שֶׁאֶקְבַּע לְךָ, אֲנִי קוֹבְעָם לְאוֹתוֹ מָקוֹם:

והקטורת אשר תעשה. אמר רבא, קטורת שפטמה לחצאין חייב, דכתיב והקטורת אשר תעשה, כל שתעשה, והא אפשר דעביד ליה פרס בשחרית ופרס בין הערבים .
(שם ה׳ א׳)
comments.sourceHeRef: תורה תמימה על התורה, שמות ל:לו:א

comments.he:
לא תעשו. אתם אין עושין אבל אחרים עושין לכם .
(ירושלמי מגילה פ"א ה"א)

comments.he:
לא תעשו לכם. לכם הוא דאסור, אבל למסרה לצבור פטור .
(כריתות ה׳ א׳)
comments.sourceHeRef: תורה תמימה על התורה, שמות ל:לו:ג

comments.he:
קודש תהיה. כל מעשיה לא יהיו אלא בקודש .
(שם שם)

sections.en: Beat some of it into powder, and put some before the Pact in the Tent of Meeting, where I will meet with you; it shall be most holy to you.
sections.he: וְשָֽׁחַקְתָּ מִמֶּנָּה הָדֵק וְנָתַתָּה מִמֶּנָּה לִפְנֵי הָעֵדֻת בְּאֹהֶל מוֹעֵד אֲשֶׁר אִוָּעֵד לְךָ שָׁמָּה קֹדֶשׁ קׇֽדָשִׁים תִּהְיֶה לָכֶֽם׃
sections.ref: Exodus 30:36

comments.en: בהטיבו WHEN HE TRIMMETH — This word is an expression for cleansing the bowls of the candelabrum from the ashes of the wicks which had burnt out during the night; and he used to clean them (the lamps) out every morning.

comments.he: בהיטיבו. לְשׁוֹן נִקּוּי הַבָּזִיכִין שֶׁל הַמְּנוֹרָה מִדֶּשֶן הַפְּתִילוֹת שֶׁנִּשְׂרְפוּ בַלַּיְלָה, וְהָיָה מְטִיבָן בְּכָל בֹּקֶר וָבֹקֶר:

comments.en: הנרת THE LAMPS — luces in old French And this is the meaning of נרות whenever it is mentioned in connection with the candelabrum, except in any passage where the term העלאה “causing to ascend” (any verbal form which is the Hiphil of עלה), which denotes lighting is used, and there it signifies “lights”, (The translation here is therefore: “when he cleans out the lamps”, not “when he trims the lights”).

comments.he: הנרת. לו"שיש בְּלַעַז, וְכֵן כָּל נֵרוֹת הָאֲמוּרוֹת בַּמְּנוֹרָה, חוּץ מִמָּקוֹם שֶׁנֶּאֱמַר שָׁם הַעֲלָאָה שֶׁהוּא לְשׁוֹן הַדְלָקָה:

comments.en: Some have the custom to say the passage of the Laver (Exodus 30:17-21), and afterwards the passage of the removal of the ashes (Leviticus 6:1-6), and afterwards the passage of the continual-offering (Numbers 28:1-8), and afterwards the passage of the Incense Altar (Exodus 30:7-10) and the passage of the spices of the Incense and its preparation (Exodus 30:34-36).
comments.he: יש נוהגין לומר פ' הכיור ואח"כ פרשת תרומת הדשן ואח"כ פ' התמיד ואח"כ פרשת מזבח מקטר קטורת ופרשת סממני הקטורת ועשייתו:

comments.he:
בבקר בבקר. הקטורת קודמת לאברים, דתניא, יוקדם דבר שנאמר בו בבקר בבקר לדבר שלא נאמר בו אלא בקר אחד בלבד .
(פסחים נ"ט א׳)
comments.sourceHeRef: תורה תמימה על התורה, שמות ל:ז:א

comments.he:
בבקר בבקר. סדור שני גזרי עצים קודם לדישון מזבח הפנימי, ואע"פ דהכא כתיב בבקר בבקר (פ׳ צו) והכא כתיב בבקר בבקר, אפילו הכי מכשיר עדיף .
(יומא ל"ג א׳)
comments.sourceHeRef: תורה תמימה על התורה, שמות ל:ז:ב

comments.he:
בבקר בבקר. חלקהו לשני בקרים [מלמד שעבודה מפסקת בין הטבת הנרות] .
(שם שם ב׳)
comments.sourceHeRef: תורה תמימה על התורה, שמות ל:ז:ג

comments.he:
בבקר בבקר. תנא ר' ישמעאל, בבקר בבקר, בא הכתוב ליתן תחום לבקרו של בקר .
(ירושלמי ברכות פ"א ה"א)
comments.sourceHeRef: תורה תמימה על התורה, שמות ל:ז:ד

comments.he:
בבקר בבקר בהיטיבו. אין מחנכין את המנורה אלא בנרות של בין הערבים, ואת המזבח בקטורת של בין הערבים, שנאמר בבקר בבקר בהטיבו את הנרות יקטירנה, ואי לאו דעביד הדלקה מאורתא הטבה בצפרא מהיכי .
(מנחות נ׳ א׳)

comments.he:
בהיטיבו. [הקטורת קודמת להטבת שתי נרות] , ומאי בהיטיבו את הנרות יקטירנה, הכי קאמר רחמנא, בעידן הטבה ההא מקטר קטורת .
(יומא י"ד ב׳)

comments.he:
את הנרות. [הטבת חמש נרות קודמת לקטורת וקטורת קודמת להטבת שתי נרות], מאי שנא דעביד חמש ברישא, כיון דאתחיל בהו עביד רובא, ונעביד שית, אמר קרא בהיטיבו את הנרות יקטירנה ואין נרות פחות משתים .
(שם ל"ג ב')

comments.en: Aaron is to offer his own bull of sin offering, to make expiation for himself and for his household.
comments.he: וְהִקְרִ֧יב אַהֲרֹ֛ן אֶת־פַּ֥ר הַחַטָּ֖את אֲשֶׁר־ל֑וֹ וְכִפֶּ֥ר בַּעֲד֖וֹ וּבְעַ֥ד בֵּיתֽוֹ׃

sections.en: As it is said: On it Aaron shall burn aromatic incense: he shall burn it every morning when he tends the lamps,
sections.he: וְנֶאֱמַר: וְהִקְטִיר עָלָיו אַהֲרֹן קְטֹרֶת סַמִּים בַּבֹּקֶר בַּבֹּקֶר בְּהֵיטִיבוֹ אֶת־הַנֵּרֹת יַקְטִירֶֽנָּה׃
sections.ref: Exodus 30:7

comments.en: ובהעלת means when he kindles them by making their flame ascend (cf. Rashi on Exodus 27:20 and on Numbers 8:2).
Speak to Aaron and say to him, “When you mount the lamps, let the seven lamps give light at the front of the lampstand.”
comments.he: דַּבֵּר֙ אֶֽל־אַהֲרֹ֔ן וְאָמַרְתָּ֖ אֵלָ֑יו בְּהַעֲלֹֽתְךָ֙ אֶת־הַנֵּרֹ֔ת אֶל־מוּל֙ פְּנֵ֣י הַמְּנוֹרָ֔ה יָאִ֖ירוּ שִׁבְעַ֥ת הַנֵּרֽוֹת׃
ובהעלת. כְּשֶׁיַּדְלִיקֵם לְהַעֲלוֹת לַהַבְתָן:

comments.en: יקטירנה HE SHALL BURN IT [A CONTINUAL INCENSE] — תמיד, “continual”, means every day regularly: a half he burnt in the morning and a half he burnt in the evening (Keritot 6b).

comments.he: יקטירנה. בְּכָל יוֹם, פְּרָס מַקְטִיר שַׁחֲרִית וּפְרָס מַקְטִיר בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם (כריתות ו'):

ובהעלת אהרן וגו'. מאי ובהעלות אהרן את הנרות יקטירנה, אילימא ברישא מדליק נרות והדר מקטיר קטורת, והתניא (כ"ז כ"א) יערך אותו אהרן ובניו מערב עד בקר, אין לך עבודה שכשרה מערב עד בקר אלא זו בלבד , אלא הכי קאמר רחמנא, בעידן הדלקה תהא מקטר קטורת .
(שם ט"ו א׳)
comments.sourceHeRef: תורה תמימה על התורה, שמות ל:ח:א

sections.en: and Aaron shall burn it at twilight when he lights the lamps—a regular incense offering before the L<small>ORD</small> throughout the ages.
sections.he: וּבְהַעֲלֹת אַהֲרֹן אֶת־הַנֵּרֹת בֵּין הָעַרְבַּיִם יַקְטִירֶנָּה קְטֹרֶת תָּמִיד לִפְנֵי יְהֹוָה לְדֹרֹתֵיכֶֽם׃
sections.ref: Exodus 30:8

sections.en:
Rabbi Yishmael says: The Torah is expounded through thirteen methods:
1) A conclusion drawn from a minor or lenient law, to a major or more strict one.
sections.he:
רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר בִּשְׁלֹשׁ עֶשְׂרֵה מִדּוֹת הַתּוֹרָה נִדְרָֽשֶׁת:
מִקַּל וָחֹֽמֶר.
sections.ref: Siddur Ashkenaz, Weekday, Shacharit, Preparatory Prayers, Korbanot, Baraita of Rabbi Yishmael 1

sections.en: 2) A clarification based on identical words or terms in the Biblical text.
sections.he: וּמִגְּזֵרָה שָׁוָה.
sections.ref: Siddur Ashkenaz, Weekday, Shacharit, Preparatory Prayers, Korbanot, Baraita of Rabbi Yishmael 2

sections.en: 3) A principle derived from one Biblical text or from two Biblical texts.
sections.he: מִבִּנְיַן אָב מִכָּתוּב אֶחָד, וּמִבִּנְיַן אָב מִשְּׁנֵי כְתוּבִים.
sections.ref: Siddur Ashkenaz, Weekday, Shacharit, Preparatory Prayers, Korbanot, Baraita of Rabbi Yishmael 3

sections.en: 4) A rule followed by a detail.
sections.he: מִכְּלָל וּפְרָט.
sections.ref: Siddur Ashkenaz, Weekday, Shacharit, Preparatory Prayers, Korbanot, Baraita of Rabbi Yishmael 4

sections.en: 5) A detail followed by a rule.
sections.he: וּמִפְּרָט וּכְלָל.
sections.ref: Siddur Ashkenaz, Weekday, Shacharit, Preparatory Prayers, Korbanot, Baraita of Rabbi Yishmael 5

sections.en: 6) A rule followed by a detail, which is in turn followed by a rule, may infer only what is similar to the detail.
sections.he: כְּלָל וּפְרָט וּכְלָל אִי אַתָּה דָן אֶלָּא כְּעֵין הַפְּרָט.
sections.ref: Siddur Ashkenaz, Weekday, Shacharit, Preparatory Prayers, Korbanot, Baraita of Rabbi Yishmael 6

sections.en: 7) When a general rule requires an explicit rule; when an explicit rule requires generalization.
sections.he: מִכְּלָל שֶׁהוּא צָרִיךְ לִפְרָט וּמִפְּרָט שֶׁהוּא צָרִיךְ לִכְלָל.
sections.ref: Siddur Ashkenaz, Weekday, Shacharit, Preparatory Prayers, Korbanot, Baraita of Rabbi Yishmael 7

sections.en: 8) Something included in a general rule, which was singled out to teach— was not singled out to teach about itself, but to teach (something new) concerning the rule as a whole.
sections.he: כָּל־דָּבָר שֶׁהָיָה בִּכְלָל וְיָצָא מִן הַכְּלָל לְלַמֵּד לֹא לְלַמֵּד עַל עַצְמוֹ יָצָא אֶלָּא לְלַמֵּד עַל הַכְּלָל כֻּלּוֹ יָצָא.
sections.ref: Siddur Ashkenaz, Weekday, Shacharit, Preparatory Prayers, Korbanot, Baraita of Rabbi Yishmael 8

sections.en: 9) Something that was included in a rule and was singled out in a case similar to its rule, —it was singled out to lessen not to increase the severity of the case.
sections.he: כָּל־דָּבָר שֶׁהָיָה בִּכְלָל וְיָצָא לִטְעֹן טֹֽעַן אֶחָד שֶׁהוּא כְעִנְיָנוֹ יָצָא לְהָקֵל וְלֹא לְהַחֲמִיר.
sections.ref: Siddur Ashkenaz, Weekday, Shacharit, Preparatory Prayers, Korbanot, Baraita of Rabbi Yishmael 9

sections.en: 10) Something that was included in a rule and was singled out in a case which is not similar to its rule, —it was singled out either to lessen or to increase the severity of the case.
sections.he: כָּל־דָּבָר שֶׁהָיָה בִּכְלָל וְיָצָא לִטְעֹן טֹֽעַן אַחֵר שֶׁלֹּא כְעִנְיָנוֹ יָצָא לְהָקֵל וּלְהַחֲמִיר.
sections.ref: Siddur Ashkenaz, Weekday, Shacharit, Preparatory Prayers, Korbanot, Baraita of Rabbi Yishmael 10

sections.en: 11) Something that was included in a rule and was singled out for a new stipulation— does not revert to its rule unless Scripture restores it to its rule expressly.
sections.he: כָּל־דָּבָר שֶׁהָיָה בִּכְלָל וְיָצָא לִדּוֹן בַּדָּבָר הֶחָדָשׁ אִי אַתָּה יָכוֹל לְהַחֲזִירוֹ לִכְלָלוֹ עַד שֶׁיַּחֲזִירֶֽנּוּ הַכָּתוּב לִכְלָלוֹ בְּפֵרוּשׁ.
sections.ref: Siddur Ashkenaz, Weekday, Shacharit, Preparatory Prayers, Korbanot, Baraita of Rabbi Yishmael 11

sections.en: 12) A matter deduced from its context, or from a subsequent expression.
sections.he: דָּבָר הַלָּמֵד מֵעִנְיָנוֹ וְדָבָר הַלָּמֵד מִסּוֹפוֹ.
sections.ref: Siddur Ashkenaz, Weekday, Shacharit, Preparatory Prayers, Korbanot, Baraita of Rabbi Yishmael 12

sections.en: 13) Also, two passages that contradict each other until a third passage reconciles them.
sections.he: וְכֵן שְׁנֵי כְתוּבִים הַמַּכְחִישִׁים זֶה אֶת־זֶה עַד שֶׁיָּבֹא הַכָּתוּב הַשְּׁלִישִׁי וְיַכְרִֽיעַ בֵּינֵיהֶם:
sections.ref: Siddur Ashkenaz, Weekday, Shacharit, Preparatory Prayers, Korbanot, Baraita of Rabbi Yishmael 13

comments.en: Then the offerings of Judah and Jerusalem shall be pleasing to the L<small>ORD</small> as in the days of yore and in the years of old.
comments.he: וְעָֽרְבָה֙ לַֽיהֹוָ֔ה מִנְחַ֥ת יְהוּדָ֖ה וִירֽוּשָׁלָ֑͏ִם כִּימֵ֣י עוֹלָ֔ם וּכְשָׁנִ֖ים קַדְמֹנִיֹּֽת׃

sections.en: May it be Your will Adonoy, our God and God of our fathers, that the Holy Temple be rebuilt speedily in our days: and grant us our share in Your Torah. And there we will serve You reverently as in the days of old, and in earlier years.
sections.he: יְהִי רָצוֹן מִלְּפָנֶֽיךָ יְהֹוָה אֱלֹהֵֽינוּ וֵאלֹהֵי אֲבוֹתֵֽינוּ שֶׁיִּבָּנֶה בֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ בִּמְהֵרָה בְיָמֵֽינוּ וְתֵן חֶלְקֵֽנוּ בְּתוֹרָתֶֽךָ: וְשָׁם נַעֲבָדְךָ בְּיִרְאָה כִּימֵי עוֹלָם וּכְשָׁנִים קַדְמוֹנִיּוֹת:
sections.ref: Siddur Ashkenaz, Weekday, Shacharit, Preparatory Prayers, Korbanot, Baraita of Rabbi Yishmael 14
